title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN IN ORBIT CLEANING TOOL FOR OPTICAL INSTRUMENTS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objectives: To develop an atomic hydrogen generator as in orbit cleaning tool for optical systems contaminated by high volatiles organic outgassing products, UV induced sticking / carbonization of molecular contamination, or radiation induced contamination. Description: Molecular contamination onto optical systems, which reduce the performance of instruments, is a phenomenon, which is known and as well observed on past and current missions. The available current method to "clean" optical systems during mission is decontamination via heating systems. The cleaning efficiency of this method is limited and not sufficient for molecular contamination sticking to a surface, polymerized or carbonized by UV light or by radiation induced contamination (RIC effect). The use of atomic hydrogen for cleaning of optical systems is a known and used method within the e.g. EUV lithography.The usage of industry available cleaning process for space missions is due to our stringed mass, power and volume requirements not feasible. But the use of quantum dot technology (in particular quantum dot pulse laser systems) could enable the usage of this established for space missions / application alleviating on-ground and in orbit cleanliness requirements. The proposed quantum dot base atomic hydrogen generator allows to build / implement an in orbit cleaning method under consideration of mass, power and volume. The principle of this method is to generating atomic hydrogen via photolysis of hydrogen with UV light ( 270 nm - 300 nm). The photolysis is a "cold" cracking process with much less heat transfer to the optical system than the already used decontamination mode cleaning method. The cleaning tool is built by a hydrogen reservoir connected with a dedicated high precision low temperature compatible valve which allows to adjust the neededhydrogen flux trough a UV transparent tube were the atomic hydrogen will be generated. The flow of atomic hydrogen is optimized onto the optical system /surface to reach high cleaning efficacy. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - requirement consolidation.- selection of a dedicated UV transparent material (e.g. Suprasil - quartz glass). - adaptation of available quantum dot UVlight systems - cleaning efficiency study of various contaminated optical surfaces.

title: Mass cytometry imaging system
description: The University of Turku plans to purchase the Fluidigm Hyperion mass cytometry imaging system to its Cytometry core facility located at Turku Bioscience. The University of Turku plans to purchase the Fluidigm Hyperion mass cytometry imaging system to its Cytometry core facility located at Turku Bioscience. This device will be integrated to our cytometry service infrastructure alongside the existing Fluidigm HeliosTM which has been in operation for services since 2018. The HyperionTM allows multiplexed imaging of up to 37 antigens simultaneously in a given sample with a high spatial resolution. This will double our capacity for HeliosTM-based single cell sorting services providing scope for largescale measurements that take weeks and months of machine time. Such measurements could not be accommodated by our existing infrastructure without this increased capacity. Similarly, it is essential that the HeliosTM devices are identical as this is a requirement for longitudinal clinical studies.

title: ARIADNA STUDY - ORGANOID INTELLIGENCE AS A RESERVOIR COMPUTING PARADIGM FOR TIME-SERIES PREDICTION - EXPRO PLUS
description: Future spacecraft will need onboard learning that stays accurate while using very little power and surviving harsh radiation. One promising route is reservoir computing: instead of training a large, power-hungry AI model, you let a complex dynamical system "naturally" transform streaming data, then train only a lightweight readout. This exploratory activity pushes that idea further by using living biology as the reservoir. The activity aims at building a compartmentalized neuronal organoidorganized with a connectome-likewiring patternand use it as a physical computing substrate to learn and predict complex, multi variable chaotic time-series. Building on recent successes with simple cell cultures and simulated whole-connectome systems, this work moves from bio inspired designs to truly biological computingtesting whether structured, connectome guided organoids can deliver robust prediction performance in environments where conventional hardware struggles.
